workflow.decision: When a security dependency appears mature, ask whether the application preserves its guarantees. Prioritize custom callbacks and pass-through exceptions rather than assuming either library reputation or the presence of a filtering call establishes safety.

For content preserved because it is classified as inert, state that trust assumption and ask whether the final consumer retains the same structure. The unresolved question is consumer interpretation, not merely whether the intermediate filter accepted the content.

Do not stop analysis at a structural filtering failure: identify the separate execution restriction before describing stronger impact. A policy checker can support configuration review, but its recommendation is not runtime validation or proof of a boundary crossing.

tools.purpose: Review whether a browser content-security policy has problematic configuration.
tools.when: The article recommends it to readers uncertain about policy correctness; it does not report the author running it. Treat findings as review leads, not enforcement proof.

handoffs.when: An application-defined filtering exception preserves content as inert, while the final consumer's interpretation remains unresolved.
handoffs.acceptance_gate: Identify both the exception and final consumer, and give distinguishable interpretation predictions. A preservation branch alone must not be classified as a demonstrated policy violation.

handoffs.when: A content-structure defect is being considered for stronger impact, but an independent execution policy remains relevant.
handoffs.acceptance_gate: Separate structural acceptance from executable capability, retain the actual policy and unknowns, and distinguish author reports or static findings from independently observed impact. A policy-linter finding cannot satisfy the execution gate.

limitations: The explanation is historical and explicitly uses CodiMD 1.2.1. Current HackMD/CodiMD behavior, dependency versions and deployed policies were not checked.

The library-maturity assessment rests on documentation and public project signals, not a proof of library correctness. Prioritizing integration review does not establish that the dependency is defect-free.
All vulnerability, execution and collaborative-editing results remain author reports. No source code, payload, attachment, demonstration video or target test was executed by this extraction.
The wormable characterization is conditional; this extraction provides no independent propagation, reliability or affected-user evidence.
The author says the latest CodiMD release was fixed and links a pull request. Neither the fix diff nor shipped/deployed artifacts were inspected, so repair and rollout are unverified here.

candidate_additions.guidance: When an application customizes a security library, review pass-through callbacks and preservation exceptions as distinct contracts. Record how each override changes default guarantees before prioritizing an upstream-library defect hypothesis.

For content exempted from filtering as inert structure, compare the filter's classification with the final consumer's interpretation of the preserved representation. Define the structural invariant and a benign contrasting observation; an intermediate inert label is not a safety guarantee.

Keep content insertion and active-content execution as separate assessment gates. Record the actual execution policy and remaining restrictions; use configuration-linter output only to prioritize review, not to claim runtime execution or stronger impact.
